Devanahalli Police Station For The Ofefnces P/U/S
420, 498A, 465, 468 R/W 34 Of Ipc Which Is Now Pending
On The File Of Additional Civil Judge And J.M.F.C.,
Devanahalli.

This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
The petitioner - accused No.3, who is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 498A, 465, 468 read with Section 34 of IPC, is before this Court.
2. The respondent No.2 lodged the FIR alleging that, the accused No.1 is the husband, and he purchased the subject vehicle in her name after obtaining finance from Mahindra Insurance Brokers.
Thereafter, by forging her signature on the cheque and the documents pertaining to the subject vehicle, pledged the same with the accused No.2 though she is the owner of the subject vehicle.
Since the accused No.1 was harassing her with regard to the subject vehicle, she started residing at her parental home.
On 31.10.2021, the accused No.1 called her on phone, and informed that, he is vacating the apartment, and when she went there, the accused No.1 assaulted her.

Hence,
requested the police to take action, and to release of the car and other documents related to the car.
The registration of FIR is impugned in this petition.
The respondent No.2 though served with notice has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1.
5.
The only allegation against the accused No.3 is that, he had threatened her by calling her on phone.

Except the said allegation, there is no allegation that, the accused herein either induced the Hemanth Gowda N vs State Of Karnataka By on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13937301/
2 respondent No.2 to pledge the documents relating to the subject vehicle with an intention to defraud her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegation of subjecting the respondent No.2 to cruelty is against the accused No.1.

Hence,
the essential elements so as to constitute the commission of the aforesaid offence are conspicuously absent, and as such, the continuation of the investigation as against the accused No.3 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.121/2021 registered by the Devanahalli Police Station insofar as it relates to the petitioner - accused No.3 is herby quashed.
